meta.what: ROUTES — named, reusable sending policies. A route says which vendors a post goes to, in what order, spread over how long, and whether it is currently paused. Routing is a policy the operator edits, not a constant buried in a fan-out script.
meta.why: Today every post takes the same path: one destination set, fired at once, 24/7. That is fine for 12 accounts and it is the thing that breaks first as the fleet grows, because every new page multiplies the load on the SAME vendor set. Vendor overload is therefore not a capacity problem to be solved later — it is a routing problem, and routing is where it has to be prevented. `/load` in genius-rt-bot already detects strain AFTER the fact (late-rate, pending count); this is the half that acts BEFORE the send.
meta.theConstraint: A vendor's real limit is not posts per day at the group level — it is RETWEETS PER MEMBER ACCOUNT PER DAY. Life Mastery is seven X accounts; a group receiving 40 requests a day is asking each of its accounts to retweet the same source ~6 times a day, which reads as automation and costs the vendor its own reach. So capacity = accounts x perAccountPerDay, and the number that saturates first is the one to watch.
meta.capacityBasis: ASSUMED, not measured. `defaultPerAccountPerDay` below is a working ceiling, not an observed one — nobody has measured the point at which a vendor account's retweets stop landing. It is declared here so routing has a number to enforce and so the assumption is visible and tunable in one place, rather than implicit in nobody checking. genius-rt-bot holds the data that would calibrate it (per-vendor confirmation rate and median time-to-confirm, already computed for /vendors): the rate falling as daily volume rises IS the saturation curve. Until that read exists, every capacity figure reports basis 'assumed'.
meta.measuredToday: Peak observed load (facts.jsonl, 38 days, 12 accounts firing): T0 16 fires in one day, which is 16 x 7 = 112 vendor-group sends through one broker. Pammy and IP peak at 9/day each. Busiest day overall: 42 vendor-sends.
meta.spontaneity: Delay, jitter and stagger are first-class. Firing eleven pages at one vendor in the same second is both a worse signal to the vendor and a worse signal to X than the same eleven spread over an hour. `stagger` spaces the vendors within one post; `jitter` moves the whole route off the clock so sends stop arriving on a machine cadence. Jitter is DETERMINISTIC per link, so re-planning a post gives the same answer instead of drifting.
meta.howToUse: routing.mjs reads this. A route is chosen per post; `default` is used when nothing is specified. Editing a route here changes behaviour with no code change — that is the point.
meta.mostTraffic: offhours — the operator's own read (2026-09-03): most threads take this lane.

measuredPerAccountLoad.what: PEAK retweets asked of ONE member account per day. Measured fires (facts.jsonl, 38 days, 12 accounts firing) divided by the vendor's known roster size. Only the CEILING is assumed — the load itself is counted.
measuredPerAccountLoad.finding: Overload is not a future scaling problem. It is already binding, and it is binding on exactly the vendors with the SMALLEST rosters, because routing by group treats a 1-account vendor and a 33-account vendor as equivalent destinations when their capacity differs 33x.
measuredPerAccountLoad.worst: GL Growth Lab is a SINGLE X account (@growthhub_, 506k) being asked to retweet 16 times a day from one source. Pammy (@_Pammy_DS_) and IP (@MindTendencies2) are single accounts at 9/day. No plausible ceiling makes those fine, and the conclusion does not depend on where the ceiling actually sits.
measuredPerAccountLoad.calibration: genius-rt-bot's /vendors leaderboard already computes confirmation rate and median time-to-confirm per vendor. If this reading is right, those five should show the worst confirm rates in the fleet — which is both the check on this model and the way to find the real ceiling.

alternation.what: t0-a and t0-b are a DISJOINT PAIR, alternated per post (or per day). Nothing in either set appears in the other.
alternation.why: Alternation is the overload fix. A single lane puts every post on the same vendors; two disjoint lanes halve what each vendor sees at identical fleet volume. Measured effect on the worst case: 16.0 -> 4.0 retweets per member account per day, a 4x reduction — and it drops every ONE-ACCOUNT vendor (gl-growth-lab, pammy, ip) out of the routine lane, which is where the load was actually concentrated.
alternation.budgetMet: Cost yes ($10.75 and $14.80, avg $12.78 — was $13.25/$14.80 before ConquerMM went free on 2026-09-08). Reach NO — 4.48M and 4.44M, about 11% short of the 5M floor. Reach is what these halves never met, and cheaper ConquerMM does not change it.
alternation.whyReachIsShort: The roster holds only 8.93M of reach below $6.50/post. Two DISJOINT 5-6M paths need 10-12M inside $30 total, and past $6.50 reach costs 3-8x more per 1k views ($0.052-$0.190 vs $0.009-$0.028). The binding constraint is the shape of the roster, not the budget.

priceOfClosingTheGap.bothAt5.5M_reachableToday: impossible within the per-account load ceiling
priceOfClosingTheGap.note: Onboarding ME (Phase 2) is worth $2.75/post at the 5.0M floor — the cheapest way to buy reach here is wiring vendors we already pay to have, not paying more per post.

alternation.watchItem: t0-b saturates at ~12 fleet accounts on Lewin (2 member accounts) — that is TODAY's account count, so B has no runway. Lewin and VOPE are retainer vendors bought for unlimited USE, but that is a billing term, not a promise their accounts can absorb more retweets per day; the X-side risk is identical whatever we pay. So their ceiling stays at the default until measured. Raising it is the single biggest lever on this pair's headroom, and it needs evidence, not a contract.
alternation.ceilingAfterCorrections: With Lewin at its stated 17/day and the pair alternating (each route carries half the fleet's posts), T0-B now caps at ~25 fleet accounts, up from 12. T0-A caps at ~18 on ConquerMM (3 accounts on the default assumed ceiling), so THE PAIR caps at ~18 — ConquerMM is the new binding vendor, and its ceiling is the modelled one, not a stated one. Worth asking ConquerMM what they can take, the way VOPE and Lewin were asked.
alternation.superseded: HISTORICAL. t0-a/t0-b were the 2026-09-03 alternation design; Sun/Moon replaced them on 09-06, and the whole pair was COLLAPSED TO ONE BLOCK on 09-08 (see whyRestore). Kept because the per-account load analysis above is still the best read the fleet has of where vendor overload actually binds, and because the 09-08 burst test says the thing alternation was built to fix is NOT what cost us reach: position inside a day's block does not move views at 2h (3,199 / 3,450 / 3,193 / 3,369 / 3,526 by quintile, n=206). Membership did. Load remains a real ceiling to plan against; it was not the 09-07 failure.

sendingWindow.confirmed: 07:00-12:00 America/New_York (operator, 2026-09-03) — the real window vendors act in, not an inherited client policy.
sendingWindow.theTension: The fleet publishes when ITS audience is awake (Saigon afternoon) and vendors retweet when THEY are awake (US morning). Eleven hours apart, so NO publish schedule satisfies both. Every thread slot in slots.mjs is 0% inside the window; only singles (13:00-22:00 SGN) overlaps, at 44%.

twoLevers.expand: Widening the window does NOT add capacity — a vendor's daily ceiling is unchanged. It adds SPACING at a given volume, which is what keeps that volume deliverable. 17 posts into 5 hours is one every 18 minutes; into 9 hours it is one every 32. Same posts, far less like a burst, to the vendor and to X.
twoLevers.decouple: The RT ping does not have to fire at publish time. Publish at the audience-optimal Saigon hour, QUEUE the ping for the next vendor window. This costs nothing, needs no vendor to change anything, and it is the only lever that actually closes the 0% overlap. planRoute({respectWindows:true}) already holds an out-of-window send; it was inert only because the window was unconfirmed. It is confirmed now.

options.note: TODAY. At 12 accounts firing this is already down to ~3 accounts of headroom.

options.why: Nearly doubles the slots (20 -> 36) and takes headroom from 15 to 27 fleet accounts, while staying inside plausible US waking hours. The cheapest real gain on the table.

options.note: The only option that COVERS the afternoon/viral thread slot (13:00-15:30 SGN), so threads could ping at publish time. But 02:00 ET is the middle of the night for a US vendor — likely not real. Decoupling gets the same result without asking anyone to work at 2am.

sendingWindow.recommendation: Do both, in this order. (1) DECOUPLE — hold out-of-window pings to the next window. Free, immediate, and it is what makes the confirmed window usable at all. (2) EXPAND to 05:00-14:00 ET if the vendors will take it: 36 slots against today's 20, and fleet headroom from 15 accounts to 27. Chasing an overlap by moving publish times is the option NOT to take — it trades the fleet's own audience timing, which is measured, for vendor convenience, which decoupling solves for nothing.

whyRecut.source: operator table, 2026-09-08 — 'GO cheap go broke type of mindset'
whyRecut.theDay: 2026-09-07 was the fleet's worst day in the window, and not because the posts were young. Age-normalised from the Growth Log, median views at 24h: 152,745 (09-04) · 88,365 (09-05) · 44,493 (09-06) · 10,472 (09-07). The gap WIDENS with age — down 34% at 2h, 46% at 6h, 75% at 12h, 76% at 24h — which is the ladder failing to fire rather than T0 alone being weak. T1+ fire rate went 33% · 38% · 12%: the T1 bar is 10,000 views inside 8 hours, and the median 09-07 post had 3,426 at 6h. It crossed 10k around the 24-hour mark, long after the gate shut. Engagement RATE rose (1.27% vs 0.56%) while impressions collapsed, which is the signature of less distribution rather than worse writing.
whyRecut.theCause: The switch armed at 07:09Z, so 09-07 carries its own control group — nine posts fired pre-switch on the old five-network T0, eight fired routed. Median views at 24h: pre-switch 37,588 (n=9) · Sun 31,069 (n=4) · Moon 1,950 (n=4), with 0 of 4 Moon posts earning T1+. Controlling for page size (each post against its own account's prior-week median at 2h, before T1 can plausibly fire) the pre-switch cohort ran at 1.12x its baseline that morning, Sun at 0.57x, Moon at 0.62x. Same day, same writers, same pipeline: the route is what moved.
whyRecut.theFinding: Moon's old T0 was the four networks that cost nothing at the margin (Lewin, VOPE, All VGNs, GL Growth Lab). It claimed 2,167,095 nominal reach — 61% of the old single T0's 3,537,349 — and returned roughly 5% of the views. Sun, essentially Life Mastery plus Lifepad, claimed 83% of the old reach and delivered about 83% of it. NOMINAL REACH PREDICTS DELIVERY FOR THE PAID NETWORKS AND NOT AT ALL FOR THE FREE ONES. The claim in the original route design that the two T0 halves 'sit within 2%' was never true in the field: they were 2.93M against 2.17M on paper and 16x apart in delivery.
whyRecut.limits: n=4 per route on a single day, one large outlier in each arm, and the 24h column is partly endogenous — a post that earns T1+ gets more views BECAUSE it earned. The 2h within-account column is the cleanest number and it still says the routed T0 delivered a little over half of what the old one did.
whyRecut.theTrade: T0 spend per post goes from ~$4.53 average (Sun $6.75 / Moon $2.30) to ~$11.08 (Sun $10.85 / Moon $11.30) — up 145%, for +68% nominal T0 reach and a far better shot at the T1 bar. At 17 posts/day that is ~$188/day, ~$5,650/month for T0 alone, ABOVE the $5,000 monthly RT budget the supply board plans against, before T1-T5. Deliberate, and the operator's call.
whyRecut.balance: With ConquerMM dark the re-cut routes are almost perfectly balanced (Sun 3,930,319 vs Moon 3,819,378 — 3%). Ticking ConquerMM on makes Moon 18% heavier (3,930,319 vs 4,649,055) and adds $2.50 to every Moon post, about $640/month at half the fleet's volume.
whyRecut.conquermm: STAYS DARK (operator, 2026-09-08). Its Config row is tiered into Moon T0 and its Routes text is correct, so ticking `Active` is the only step left whenever the call changes — no code, no push. The reason to wait: the 3% balance is better than the 18% one, and the re-cut's own effect should be read on the next day's numbers before another variable is added. routes-push.mjs reports it as a finding on every run so it cannot be forgotten.
whyRecut.supply: Reported, not acted on (operator, 2026-09-08). T0 fires on EVERY post, so promoting a vendor into T0 turns an occasional cost into a daily one and burns its package at roughly half the fleet's volume. At the re-cut: EnergyUp 102/99 (over) and Lifepad 28 left are in Moon T0; GL Growth Lab 62 left and ME 69 left are in Sun T0; Hey Brother 30/30 and YK 2 left sit at T3/T5. `vendor-supply.mjs` prints the board and its daily cron raises the reorder alert.
whyRecut.pammy: Paused on the bot from 2026-09-06 to 2026-09-08 while Active in Config: PI billed itself for 11 T2 fires ($132) the bot never forwarded (8 on 09-06, 2 on 09-07, 1 on 09-08). Resumed by the operator, now 24/50. This class of failure is silent on our side — the Fuel Log records a fire, the money leaves, nothing errors — and `vendor-reconcile.mjs` plus the bot's `/vendor-status` `paused` flag are the two reads that catch it.

tierProposal.status: WITHDRAWN as a reordering proposal — see RETRACTED. The structural observations below still hold because they do not depend on realisation: account counts, prices, nominal reach, and which vendors have never fired. Nothing reads this file.
tierProposal.theFinding: The paid ladder is not ordered. Cost per 1k expected views by tier today: T1 $0.153, T2 $0.063, T3 $0.024, T4 $0.190, T5 $0.084, T6 $0.073. It escalates from near-worst value to best and back to worst. A ladder should exhaust cheap reach first and escalate into expensive reach only when a post earns it; this one buys in essentially random order.
tierProposal.theWorstPart: T1 fired 192 times — more than every other tier combined — and it is the second-worst value on the board at $0.153/1k. It is also Pammy + IP, two SINGLE-ACCOUNT vendors, which is precisely why they measure at 9 retweets per member account per day. The most-fired tier was built from the two vendors least able to carry it.
principles: ORDER BY MARGINAL EFFICIENCY. Each deeper tier should be WORSE value per 1k than the one before, because cheap reach is exhausted first. The proposed ladder is monotonic (0.025 -> 0.037 -> 0.052 -> 0.073 -> 0.083 -> 0.168); today's is not ordered at all.
DEEP ROSTERS GO WHERE THE FIRING IS. T1 carries ~60% of paid fires, so it needs accounts, not just reach. 10 accounts instead of 2.

SINGLE-ACCOUNT VENDORS BELONG AT THE BOTTOM. Pammy, IP and Navalism (1 account each) move to T6, where they fire ~twice a month instead of 192 times. That fixes the measured 9 RT/acct/day at its source rather than capping it afterwards.
USE THE VENDORS NOTHING USES. EU ($0.028) and Pst Cll ($0.037) are cheaper per 1k than everything currently in T2, T4, T5 and T6, and have never fired.
tierProposal.headline: T1 — the tier that fires more than all others combined — goes from $22.00 / 758,493 reach / 2 accounts / $0.153 per 1k to $12.80 / 2,652,893 / 10 accounts / $0.025 per 1k. 42% cheaper, 3.5x the reach, 5x the accounts, 6x the value. The full climb costs $10.30 more (+7%) for 1.65M more reach (+17%) and 16 more member accounts (+31%).
caveats: @Wordofwise_ (220,884) is in BOTH ml and eu, so a full T1->T4 climb would ask that one account to retweet the same post twice. Minor, but it is the only duplicate a climb can hit.
ME (7 accounts, 1.43M, $0.023/1k) would be the best vendor on the entire paid ladder and is UNUSED because it has no Airtable Config row. Onboarding it beats every tier change here.
Reach is nominal follower count, not impressions. docs/unit-economics.md measured ~19% realisation on T1, so treat per-1k figures as a comparison between vendors, never a forecast.
Tier THRESHOLDS (the velocity at which a post escalates) are untouched by this. It re-assigns which vendors sit in which tier, not when a tier fires.
tierProposal.howToApply: Edit the `Tier` field on each vendor row in the Airtable Config table (TABLES.config). vendor-snapshot.mjs records the change in Vendor Config History and alerts on it, so the before/after is preserved automatically. Revert is the same edit backwards.
tierProposal.RETRACTED: The 'ladder is inverted' claim is WITHDRAWN (operator, 2026-09-03). It rested on ranking vendors by $/1k expected views, and that ranking is not supported: the 19% realisation constant behind it was measured on Pammy + IP, who retweet each post 15-30 times, and was then applied to vendors that retweet once. That flatters every single-retweet vendor and penalises exactly the two it was calibrated on. T1's $0.169/1k is a MEASUREMENT; every other per-1k figure in the 'current' and 'proposed' blocks below is a model resting on a borrowed constant. The reordering they justify is therefore not justified. Kept for its inputs, not its conclusion.
whatStillHolds: Pammy and IP are ONE X account each. Whatever their delivery model, a single account is a single point of failure and a hard capacity ceiling.
EU (7 accounts, $4.30) and Pst Cll (9 accounts, $6.00) have NEVER fired, at any tier. That is unused inventory regardless of how reach is valued.

ME (7 accounts, 1.43M, $6.30, all seven live) versus ML (33 accounts, 2.89M, $40, five of which have ZERO followers so 28 are live): ME is 3.1x more nominal reach per dollar. Both are assumed one retweet per post, so this comparison does NOT depend on the realisation constant. The operator's read is right.
@Wordofwise_ (220,884) sits in both ML and EU, so a climb touching both asks one account to retweet the same post twice.

proposedRevision.onlyChangeIStandBehind: Put ME above ML. Same delivery model on both sides, so the comparison is clean: ME gives 227k nominal reach per dollar against ML's 72k, and every one of ME's seven accounts is live where five of ML's thirty-three are empty. ME is blocked only by having no Airtable Config row.
proposedRevision.everythingElse: Needs a measured realisation figure for a single-retweet vendor before it is more than a guess.

tierTriggers.source: n8n 'Fuel the Fire (241)' workflow X0OzDwI0XluxEEtO, node `Check Threshold`. v2 LADDER PUBLISHED 2026-09-05T04:55Z (active version dcaf1857) — the operator's spreadsheet ladder with roster prices, applied as written. The pre-v2 values are in git history (routes.json before this commit) and in the Fuel Log field description.
tierTriggers.note: The TIERS array is EDITED FROM THE COMMAND CENTER — the dashboard rewrites it in place, so it is operator-tunable without touching n8n.
tierTriggers.condition: earns = (views >= minViews AND risePerHr >= minRise) OR (riseAlone != null AND risePerHr >= riseAlone)

mechanics.rise: Velocity over a FIXED ~1h window (riseWindowMin, default 60), measured against the sample ~1h old — deliberately cadence-independent, so polling faster cannot inflate velocity and fire a tier on a batched view-counter flush.
mechanics.andVsOr: T1-T2 are pure AND: big AND still climbing, so a plateaued post never burns the cheap early tiers. T3-T6 add a velocity-only escape so a genuine rocket escalates before it clears the view bar.
mechanics.earnedVsQualified: `earned` latches as a monotonic high-water mark for the timeline. SENDS gate on `qualified` — tiers met right now — so a decelerated post never fires a tier it no longer meets.
mechanics.sendOnce: Per vendor network per post (sd.sent). A vendor sees a given post at most once.
mechanics.noHold: Fires immediately on tier-earn; the business-hours hold was removed Jun 2026.
mechanics.seeding: On first run after deploy it marks qualifying networks as already-sent, so a redeploy never blasts a backlog.
mechanics.gc: State dropped for posts unseen in 72h.
mechanics.t0: T0 is NOT in this ladder by design. The RT Bridge's ping IS the T0 boost on the same vendor chat id, so a T0 row here would double-send and double-bill; T0 spend is recorded by the Bridge instead.
mechanics.activeOnly: `Get Vendor Config` returns Active rows only, and rows without a Chat ID are filtered out. A threshold with no active vendor mapped to it is unreachable — which is why T4-T6 cannot fire today.

observations: The T1->T2 cliff is the velocity bar, not views: minRise jumps 5,000 -> 40,000/hr, an 8x step, while views only go 17,000 -> 50,000. That gap is the likeliest reason T1 fired 192 times and T2 only 56.
T2->T3 raises rise by just 40,000 -> 50,000/hr, so the ladder's hardest single step sits between T1 and T2 rather than deeper where the money is.
T4, T5 and T6 have thresholds but no ACTIVE vendor rows, so those conditions cannot fire regardless of how a post performs.

freshnessGate.applied: v1 (12/12/18/18/18/18h) saved 2026-09-05T03:05Z and PUBLISHED 04:00Z; v2 windows (8/8/8/12/16h, the operator's) PUBLISHED 2026-09-05T04:55Z with the v2 thresholds. n8n keeps a draft apart from the active version — the earlier 'LIVE' claim covered the draft only; nothing ran with any gate before 04:00Z.
freshnessGate.rationale: Operator: a late retweet does not move a post the way an early one does, so a tier not earned inside its window is not worth buying at all.
freshnessGate.assumption: The operator specified T1/T2 at 12h and 'T3 and 3' at 18h; read as T3 THROUGH T6 at 18h. If T5/T6 were meant to keep a longer window, MAX_AGE_H is one line to change.
design: MAX_AGE_H is a SEPARATE constant, not a 5th element inside TIERS. The Command Center rewrites the TIERS array in place, so a 5th element would be silently dropped the next time the dashboard saves.

It gates QUALIFIED only, never EARNED. `earned` stays the age-independent high-water mark so the timeline still records what a post achieved; `qualified` is what sends key off, so an out-of-window tier is recorded and simply never bought.

Growth rows gained `tiersTooLate` — tiers that met the views/velocity bar but missed their window. That is the audit trail for whether the gate is cutting the right spend, and it is the number to watch for a week before tightening or loosening it.
freshnessGate.verified: Draft read back byte-identical to the reviewed patch; the four changed nodes (Check Threshold, Build Broadcasts, Track Fuel Cards, Update Fuel Lift) diffed against the previously active version showed only the intended edits; published; activeVersionId now equals versionId.
freshnessGate.worked_example: A post at 200,000 views rising 55,000/hr earns T1+T2+T3. At 15h it now fires T3 ONLY — the two cheap tiers are past their 12h window. At 20h it fires nothing.
freshnessGate.concernRaised: 8h on T1/T2 cuts late accelerators (backtest: 28 posts, median final 163k). Raised 2026-09-05, not taken; a 12h gate is a one-line change to MAX_AGE_H.

ladderVersioning.question: How to tell which threads ran under the old ladder (operator, 2026-09-05).
ladderVersioning.alreadyPossible: By DATE, today, with no schema change. Every Fuel Log row carries `First Fired` and `Last Fired`, and `Tier Breakdown` already records vendor + price + reach + timestamp per fire — so what each thread actually bought is on the row. The freshness gate went live 2026-09-05T04:00Z (published; saved 03:05Z); anything fired before that ran the old rules. vendor-snapshot.mjs independently writes a full JSON roster Snapshot to Vendor Config History whenever config changes, so the ladder's shape at any past moment is recoverable too.
ladderVersioning.recommended: Add a `Ladder Version` single-line-text field to the Fuel Log and have the Build Log node stamp it at fire time. BLANK MEANS OLD SYSTEM — no backfill needed, and the cut is exact rather than inferred from a timestamp. Filter or group by it in any view.
ladderVersioning.notDoneYet: The field does not exist. Writing to a missing Airtable field fails the node with UNKNOWN_FIELD_NAME, so the field must be created BEFORE the n8n stamp is wired — two steps, in that order, or Fuel the Fire starts erroring on every fire.

backtest.data: Growth Log, 21,415 hourly snapshots across 985 posts, 2026-06-29 -> 2026-09-05. Every snapshot replayed against both ladders; a tier counts as earned if any snapshot inside its age window meets the condition.
backtest.whereTheSavingIs: T0 on every post ($8,471 -> $4,630) and T1 ($5,390 -> $1,648). T2 spend RISES ($804 -> $1,870) because the looser 20k/14k bar fires Pammy+IP more often, and T4/T5 now cost money where they were switched off.

revisedSpend.note: roster prices, Lifepad in T1. T1 spend rises $1,648 -> $2,416 for 1.56M more reach and 7 more accounts per fire.

supported: The early-qualification thesis: median final views fall monotonically with age at first qualification (248k -> 123k -> 106k -> 73k), and nothing qualifies after 24h.
Raising T1's velocity bar 5k -> 7k cleanly removes weak posts (median final ~63k).
T2 under the new rules lands on genuinely big posts (median final 521k) — Pammy+IP's repeat retweets go where they count.
Views 10/20/40/80/160k and velocity 7/14/28/56/90k are a clean doubling; the old ladder's 8x T1->T2 velocity cliff is gone.
No duplicate X accounts anywhere in the new ladder (a side effect of dropping ConquerMM and ML).
pushback: 8h on T1 is aggressive. The 28 posts it cuts as 'too late' have a median final of 163k — comparable to the 189k of posts kept. They are late accelerators, not duds. A 12h gate keeps them and still drops the 12-24h group (73k median), for roughly $290 more across the period.
T2's 40k/hr escape does nothing in 985 posts. Harmless, but not a lever.
GL Growth Lab is one X account in the default lane at 16 retweets a day — unchanged by this proposal.
read.cannotTest: The backtest shows late-qualifying posts are SMALLER. It cannot show whether a late retweet ADDS less to a given post — that needs per-fire lift, which T0 has never had and the tiers only partly have.

blockers: T1 = Hey Brother + ME + Lifepad. Only Lifepad has a Config row, so T1 fires on one of its three networks until ME and Hey Brother are onboarded — a partial, not a hole.

T0's five networks are not the broker's seven (Lifepad moved to T1, ConquerMM gone). Either the broker sells this set at ~$4.55 — a price edit on the existing row — or this is direct sending, which needs the RT Bridge changed and T0 added to the Fuel the Fire ladder. Need to know which.

whyRestore.source: operator, 2026-09-08 — "keeping it as one block" · "Recreate t0 exactly as that Boosting GA Bridge (T0) ... with path B" · "ConquerMM is free btw" · "ME to t2 (after Pammy and IP)"
whyRestore.theQuestion: What was the T0 that worked? Reconstructed from what each post BILLED on its Fuel Log `Tier Breakdown` lines, not from any document.
whyRestore.theRegimes: Every T0 the fleet has run, with the share of posts that crossed 10,000 views inside 8 hours — which is literally the T1 gate: 08-15 → 09-04, ONE broker line (Boosting GA Bridge), $8.60, 5.89M nominal → 78% crossed (n=194). 09-05 → 09-07, direct five (GL, Life Mastery, Lewin, VOPE, VGNs), $4.55, 3.54M → 50% (n=38). 09-07 Sun (Life Mastery, Lifepad), $6.75, 2.93M → 33% (n=9). 09-07 Moon (GL, Lewin, VOPE, VGNs), $2.30, 2.17M → 20% (n=5). 09-08 Sun, $10.85, 3.93M → 25% (n=4). 09-08 Moon, $8.80, 3.82M → 67% (n=3).
whyRestore.theCause: On 2026-09-05 the Bridge flipped from broker mode to a direct fan-out and DROPPED TWO OF THE SEVEN — ConquerMM (829,677) and Lifepad (1,557,200), both operator calls recorded in vendors.json bundles.t0Direct.droppedFromBrokerSet. That is 2,386,877 of nominal reach against the 2,352,651 the bundle lost (5,890,000 → 3,537,349). T0 gave up 40% of its reach to save about $4 a post, and the crossing rate went 78% → 50% the same day. The Sun/Moon split then halved what was left. This is the mechanism behind the operator's "go cheap go broke", and it is dated two days BEFORE the split.
whyRestore.notAWeekend: The 09-05 → 09-07 window is Fri-Sun, so weekday was controlled inside the bundle era: Fri-Sun crossed 79% (n=71) against Mon-Thu 77% (n=128). Nothing there.
whyRestore.notTheBurst: The operator's other candidate — "all the posts come at once and that overwhelms the vendors" — was tested directly and does NOT hold. Ranking each post by its position inside its own day's block (21 days, n=206), median views at 2h by quintile: 3,199 / 3,450 / 3,193 / 3,369 / 3,526. Flat. HONEST LIMIT: the block is only ~113 minutes wide, so what is tested is "within two hours", not a genuinely spread day.
whyRestore.brokerOrDirect: It did not matter. The direct five at 3.54M is the SAME five networks the broker fired, sent directly: 60% of the reach returning 64% of the crossing rate. Membership moved the number; the sending mechanism did not. So Path B (rebuild direct) is expected to land where the broker did, and it keeps the per-network confirms and one ledger line each that the bundle never gave.
whyRestore.theLadder: T0 = the bundle's own seven. T1 = Pammy + IP, which is a RESTORATION: they fired 68 times each at T1 through the 78% era and only 12 times each at T2 after. T2 = ME (operator: "ME to t2, after Pammy and IP"). EU is not one of the seven and the operator did not place it; it sits at T3, which is where the pre-09-05 ladder had it (alongside Pst Cll) — CHANGE THIS FIRST if the operator meant otherwise.
whyRestore.cost: T0 $9.05 / 5,924,226 nominal. Against the broker's $8.60 for the same seven, the 45c difference is Lifepad alone: our Config row bills $4.50 where the T0 arrangement was $4.00. The whole ladder if a post climbs every rung: $83.95 (T0 9.05 + T1 22.00 + T2 6.30 + T3 14.60 + T4 20.00 + T5 12.00).
whyRestore.conquermm: FREE, and ACTIVE (operator, 2026-09-08). This SUPERSEDES the 2026-09-03 answer recorded in vendors.json bundles.t0.memberCostWhy, which had it at $2.50 per ping and incremental — that figure is why the direct rebuild was priced at $11.10 and why whyRecut left the row dark. At $0 it is the cheapest 829,677 on the roster and there is no reason to hold it. WORTH KNOWING: ConquerMM has never once appeared on a Fuel Log line — 0 in the entire table — so its reach is an unverified number on a Config row. Direct sending is what will finally measure it.
whyRestore.reachIsSizeNotMembership: The seven sum to 5,924,226 against the 5,890,000 on the broker's Config row, 0.58% apart — which is WEAKER evidence than it looks and must not be read as proof of membership. The bot's off-hours six (Life Mastery, GL, VOPE, ME, All-VGNs, Lifepad) sums to 5,897,292, 0.12% away and CLOSER, because ME (1,428,506) is within 2% of ConquerMM + Lewin (1,455,440). Membership rests on the operator's own list of 2026-08-18, recorded in vendors.json bundles.t0.compositionCheck. The cost reconstruction is exact; the membership inference is the operator's list.
whyRestore.theBroker: Left INACTIVE. Re-ticking "Vendor – Boosting GA Bridge (T0)" would restore the same seven for $8.60 in one checkbox — the Fuel Gate reverts automatically, because a T0 row sharing the RT chat is broker mode and wins. The operator chose direct: 45c a post buys per-network delivery confirms, one Fuel Log line each, and the ability to drop a member that never delivers. T0 has had a charge and a shrug since 2026-08-14; this is the change that ends that.
whyRestore.supply: UNCHANGED AND STILL BINDING. T0 fires on EVERY post, so all seven now burn at full fleet volume rather than half of it. Lifepad had 28 left at the re-cut and is now in T0 on every post — roughly three days. GL Growth Lab 62 left. ConquerMM has no measured package at all. `vendor-supply.mjs` prints the board; this restore makes its reorder alert more urgent, not less.

whyBlocks.source: operator table + follow-up, 2026-09-08 — "24 posts per day, smart optimal spacing" · "spread out our current posts across these three timelines: the sun, the cloud, the moon" · "I actually believe in my thesis, so we are going to invert for the sun because we are using proven threads and we are posting in hours where there is not enough competition"
whyBlocks.whatChanged: A route is no longer a hash of the post's status id — it is the BLOCK ITS PUBLISH TIME FALLS IN. The Sun/Moon alternation this replaces was collapsed to one block earlier the same day (whyRestore); the per-route tier machinery it left behind is what makes this a small change instead of a rewrite.
whyBlocks.thePublishTimeRule: CRITICAL, and the one thing that would silently misbill: the block must be drawn from the post's PUBLISH time, never from the clock at evaluation time. Fuel the Fire checks T1 hours after publish — a 01:00 Sun post evaluated at 09:00 would draw Cloud and fire the wrong tier set at the wrong prices. Check-Threshold carries `createdMs` and the Bridge carries `published_at`, so both workflows can agree on the same instant.
whyBlocks.hoursAreData: The block boundaries live in the `Vendor Routes` Config row's `Routes` text — "Sun 01:00-05:00 · Cloud 11:00-16:00 · Moon 17:00-22:00" — so moving a block is an Airtable edit, not a deploy. Only the parser deploys. Saigon is UTC+7 with no DST, so the offset is a constant in the helper.
whyBlocks.outsideEveryBlock: A post published outside all three blocks draws NO route and runs the plain `Tier` column, which is the restored standard ladder. That is the safe default: a hand-placed draft at 08:00 gets the seven, not nothing.
whyBlocks.whyOnlySunCarriesRoutesText: Seven rows carry Routes text, not twenty-four: routesTextFor emits it for any vendor whose tier differs across the blocks, and names all three explicitly — Pammy and IP get "Sun T0 · Cloud T1 · Moon T1", and VOPE, Lewin, All VGNs, ConquerMM and Lifepad get "Sun T1 · Cloud T0 · Moon T0". Life Mastery and GL Growth Lab are T0 in every block and carry nothing. (An earlier draft of this note said only Sun needed naming; the derivation names all three, which is more explicit and survives a block rename.)
whyBlocks.economics: Sun T0 is $26.55/post against the standard $9.05, and T0 fires on EVERY post. At 6 Sun posts a day that is ~+$67/day net of the T1 saving, ~+$2,000/month. The operator accepted this deliberately.
whyBlocks.theEvidenceForAndAgainst: FOR: the block is 01:00-05:00, hours the fleet has never posted in, carrying proven bodies; and a T0 that is awake is the whole lesson of 2026-09-05, where reach that did not deliver cost the fleet its ignition. AGAINST: at 04:00-05:00 Saigon — the two hours of this block we HAVE measured — the standard T0 crossed 10k on 67-100% of posts and 04:00 is the highest $/post hour on the board, which is not what a sleeping T0 looks like. 01:00-03:59 is n=0. The operator knows the vendors; the file records both readings.
whyBlocks.theRealRisk: SUPPLY, not timing. At 24 threads/day Lifepad has ~1.1 days of stock and Pammy ~1.9 — and the inversion makes Pammy fire 12.5x/day (Sun T0 plus Cloud/Moon T1) rather than 6. Operator chose to switch now and accept the fade. If they empty mid-experiment the Sun read is unreadable, so `vendor-supply.mjs` is the thing to watch daily.
whyBlocks.whatWouldSettleIt: Nothing records WHICH vendors are awake WHEN. `inSendingWindow()` already accepts a per-vendor `window` and falls back to the fleet-wide 07:00-12:00 ET, reporting basis "unmeasured" — and not one vendor has one filled in. Filling those turns this inversion from a hand-picked set into a rule the system enforces for every block, and lets `splitByWindow` HOLD an off-hours send instead of firing it into a sleeping group.
whyBlocks.blockBoundaries: Start is inclusive, Finish EXCLUSIVE. A post at exactly 05:00, 16:00 or 22:00 Saigon falls outside every block and runs the plain Tier column, which matches how the operator's table reads Start/Finish and keeps the three blocks from overlapping by a minute.
whyBlocks.retiredSun: 2026-09-26 (owner): the live row is "Cloud 11:00-17:00 · Moon 17:00-23:30". Sun is off it and Cloud runs to 17:00. Cloud and Moon run one ladder, so no vendor row needs Routes text any more (routesTextFor returns "" for all of them). The per-block machinery stays in the nodes, pinned by tests/bridge-routes.test.mjs with the retired Sun inversion as its fixture, so an inverted block can come back as an Airtable edit.
